kjv: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
note: TR adds the doxology "hoti sou estin he basileia kai he dynamis kai he doxa eis tous aionas amen", a liturgical ending (cf. Didache 8.2, 1 Chr 29:11) absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae and the early fathers' commentaries on the prayer.

mine: deliver us from the evil one
note: apo tou ponerou may be neuter ("evil") or masculine ("the evil one", as in 13:19, 38); Matthew's usage favours the personal sense.
TR adds "en to phanero" ("openly") here and in 6:6, 6:18, making the public reward explicit; absent from the earliest manuscripts.

kjv: that ye do not your alms before men
mine: Beware of practicing your righteousness before other people
note: TR reads eleemosynen ("alms"); the earliest manuscripts read dikaiosynen ("righteousness"), a heading for almsgiving, prayer and fasting (6:2-18).

kjv: Give us this day our daily bread
mine: Give us today our bread for the coming day
note: epiousios is a rare word of uncertain meaning: "for the coming day", "necessary for existence" or "daily"; "daily" follows the Old Latin quotidianum.

kjv: can add one cubit unto his stature
mine: can add a single hour to his span of life
note: helikia can mean stature or age/lifespan; a cubit (c. 45 cm) added to one's height would be no small thing, so a measure of time fits the context of anxiety about life.
